title: Find process by command arguments
summary: Use pgrep with the -f flag to find processes based on their full command line arguments, not just the executable name. This helps distinguish between multiple instances of the same program running with different options.

steps.explain: Use the -f flag to match against the full argument list of the process, rather than just the process name. This is useful when you need to find a specific instance of a program started with certain parameters.

placeholders.name: PARAMETER
placeholders.description: A specific argument or flag used when starting the process

alternatives.explain: Show the PID along with the full command line arguments for each match.

placeholders.name: PROCESS_NAME
placeholders.description: The name of the executable or part of the command line
